title: Head of Product Design
description: <div class="description content"> <p><a href="https://www.thoughtworks.com/">Thoughtworks</a> is a global technology consultancy that integrates design, engineering and AI to drive digital innovation. We are over 10,000 people strong across 47 offices in 18 countries. For 30+ years, we’ve delivered extraordinary impact together with our clients by helping them solve complex business problems with technology and culture as the differentiator.<br><br>Thoughtworks.com is one of our most important customer-facing products, helping clients discover our expertise, explore evidence of our impact and take the next step with us. It also helps job seekers explore opportunities and gives search engines and AI assistants an accurate, trusted understanding of who we are and what we do.</p> <p>Today, fragmented ownership across Marketing limits our ability to deliver connected customer journeys, maintain consistent quality and continuously improve performance.</p> <p>We’re looking for a Head of Product Design to change that. You’ll lead Thoughtworks.com as a digital product, translating our go-to-market and employer brand strategies into seamless experiences for customers, job seekers and AI agents. You’ll own the website strategy, roadmap, customer journeys, publishing model and content and design quality. You'll also shape experiences across connected channels, including email through Knak and events through Splash, while influencing the internal workflows that drive quality, consistency and speed.</p> <p>This is a hands-on, player-coach role for someone who can think strategically and deliver at every level, from defining roadmaps and improving customer journeys to refining copy, reviewing designs, interpreting performance data and making launch decisions.</p> </div> <h2 id="job-responsibilities">Job responsibilities</h2> <div class="job-responsibilities content"> <ul> <li> <h3>Website product strategy</h3> <ul> <li>Set the product vision, principles and roadmap for Thoughtworks.com</li> <li>Prioritize work around customer and business outcomes rather than requests for individual pages</li> <li>Connect the website roadmap to Thoughtworks’ go-to-market priorities, propositions and major company launches.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Customer journeys and experience</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Build a deep understanding of our audiences, including enterprise buyers, technology leaders, practitioners, partners, prospective employees and alumni community</li> <li>Design connected journeys that help people move from a question/problem/need to relevant services, expertise, evidence and action, where the site fuels journeys on AI platforms that might never have users interact with our site</li> <li>Use customer research, website data and market insight to identify friction and opportunities</li> <li>Ensure the core website, event pages and email experiences work together where they form part of the same journey.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Narrative, copy and content quality</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Own the quality and coherence of the website narrative, copy and information architecture</li> <li>Translate complex technology services and Thoughtworks expertise into clear, credible experiences for different audiences</li> <li>Challenge unclear propositions, duplicated content, unsupported claims and pages that do not serve a defined customer need</li> <li>Work with the central Content team, service-line marketers and subject-matter experts, while keeping accountability for how content works within the overall experience</li> <li>Work with content operations to establish reusable content patterns, editorial standards and clear ownership for maintaining important content.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Experiences for people and agents</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Ensure the website is useful and understandable to human visitors, search engines and AI assistants</li> <li>Partner with the SEO and LLM Discoverability Lead to improve how Thoughtworks is found, interpreted and represented to support buyers in their decision making process</li> <li>Shape requirements for structured content, metadata, evidence, content relationships and reusable information</li> <li>Balance machine readability with strong human storytelling, accessibility and brand expression.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Publishing model for the AI era</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Own the spec for redesigning the publishing workflow from brief through design, production, approval, release and ongoing improvement</li> <li>Work with the GTM tech and Global IT teams to replace manual, error-prone production with reusable patterns, clearer decision rights and proportionate automation</li> <li>Identify where AI can improve research, prototyping, content preparation, metadata, accessibility checks, quality assurance and content maintenance</li> <li>Turn good judgment into practical standards, templates, playbooks and automated checks</li> <li>Build a model that allows teams to move faster without lowering the quality bar or creating uncontrolled publishing.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Design quality and experimentation</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Set the direction and quality bar for UX, UI, interaction design and the website design system</li> <li>Use qualitative and quantitative evidence to improve journeys, messaging and conversion over time</li> <li>Sign off on experience quality before major launches.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Team and agency leadership</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Lead and develop a multidisciplinary team spanning product design, experience production, transformation and discoverability</li> <li>Give people clear outcomes, decision rights, constructive feedback and room to do excellent work</li> <li>Build an effective working model with the central Content team, GTM technology, Global IT and service-line marketers.</li> </ul> </li> </ul> </div> <h2 id="job-qualifications">Job qualifications</h2> <div class="job-qualifications content"> <h3 id="technical-skills">Technical Skills</h3> <div class="qualifications inner-content"> <ul> <li>10 - 15 years experience leading digital products, customer experiences, service design or product design</li> <li>A strong record of turning customer insight and business strategy into coherent end-to-end experiences</li> <li>Excellent judgment across product, UX, content and design, with the ability to recognize and explain what good looks like</li> <li>Strong writing and editorial instincts, including the confidence to simplify complex ideas and challenge unclear copy</li> <li>Experience working with marketing, product, design, engineering and senior business stakeholders</li> <li>Commercial understanding and the ability to connect digital experience decisions to go-to-market outcomes</li> <li>Systems thinking, including experience creating reusable patterns, design systems, operating models or publishing frameworks</li> <li>Practical understanding of search, structured content and how AI assistants discover and interpret information</li> <li>Experience using AI tools to improve how work is researched, designed, produced or assured</li> <li>The ability to operate in ambiguity, make difficult prioritization decisions and move from strategy to delivery</li> <li>Evidence of leading and coaching people or multidisciplinary teams.</li> </ul> </div> <h3 id="professional-skills">Professional Skills</h3> <div class="skills inner-content"> <ul> <li>You have a natural ability to establish and nurture relationships with senior leaders across the organization</li> <li>You have excellent context-switching capabilities</li> <li>You thrive in situations where you are given little to no direction and have the ability to lead, organize and deliver commitments on time and within budget</li> <li>You’re resilient in ambiguous situations and can adapt your role to approach challenges from multiple perspectives. You don’t shy away from risks, instead you take them on and skillfully manage them</li> <li>You’re empathetic and use this ability to build solid working relationships and resolve issues quickly and thoughtfully</li> </ul> </div> </div> <h2 id="important-things">Other things to know</h2> <div class="important-things content"> <h3>Learning &amp; Development</h3> <div class="inner-content"> <p>There is no one-size-fits-all career path at Thoughtworks: however you want to develop your career is entirely up to you. But we also balance autonomy with the strength of our cultivation culture. This means your career is supported by interactive tools, numerous development programs and teammates who want to help you grow. We see value in helping each other be our best and that extends to empowering our employees in their career journeys.</p> </div> </div> <h2 id="responsible-ai-use">Responsible Use of AI in Recruitment</h2> <div class="responsible-ai-use content"> <p>At Thoughtworks, we use AI tools to support our recruitment team with administrative tasks such as drafting communications, scheduling interviews and writing job descriptions.<br><br>Crucially, our AI tools do not screen, assess, rank or make hiring decisions. Every application is reviewed by our team and all selection decisions are made exclusively by our interviewers and hiring managers.<br><br>We are committed to fairness and responsible AI. We actively manage our AI systems by testing, monitoring for biased outcomes and implementing mitigation measures. We hold our third-party vendors to these same high standards through a rigorous governance process. For additional information, please see our full <a href="https://www.thoughtworks.com/careers/ai-policy-for-recruitment" target="_blank">Thoughtworks AI Policy for Recruitment</a>.</p> </div> <h2 id="about">About Thoughtworks</h2> <div class="about content"> <p>Thoughtworks is a dynamic and inclusive community of bright and supportive colleagues who are revolutionizing tech. As a leading technology consultancy, we’re pushing boundaries through our purposeful and impactful work. For 30+ years, we’ve delivered extraordinary impact together with our clients by helping them solve complex business problems with technology as the differentiator. Bring your brilliant expertise and commitment for continuous learning to Thoughtworks. Together, let’s be extraordinary.</p> </div> <p style="display: none;">#LI-Hybrid</p><div class="content-conclusion"><p style="text-align: center;"><a href="https://www.thoughtworks.com/careers/ai-policy-for-recruitment">See here our AI policy.</a></p></div> Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Data Center Architect
description: Role Profile Job Title: Data Centre Architect Reports to: Head of Data Centre Development Location: UK hybrid Company Overview: Radiant is redefining how AI infrastructure is built. We design and operate AI-native cloud platforms engineered for sovereignty, performance, and scale. Our infrastructure powers GPU-native workloads, multi-tenant control planes, and high-performance AI systems designed for the most demanding environments. We are not building a generic cloud. We are building purpose-built AI infrastructure — from powered land, to compute, to software. As we scale, we’re building this organisation from the ground up. We’re looking for people who’d rather build the playbook than inherit one — who are comfortable doing the work themselves as well as directing others, and who can adapt as fast as our strategy does. This is a startup model: attitude and adaptability matter more to us than years of experience or the size of team you’ve previously managed. This is a senior individual contributor role with authority to sign off technical schedules, working with cluster and network architects, NVIDIA and other OEM engineers, colocation provider engineering and sales teams, and the internal Procurement, Legal, Finance and Site Operations teams. What You’ll Do You will be the single technical authority between our GPU-as-a-service business and the colocation providers that host our NVIDIA clusters. You turn cluster architecture and OEM requirements into a precise, contractable statement of work (SOW) for the data centre white space, then hold the provider to it through design, installation and acceptance. We are growing from tens of megawatts to hundreds, on rack-scale liquid-cooled platforms at 130 kW per rack and rising to 200 kW and beyond. Mistakes in power, cooling or fibre specification show up as stranded capacity, delayed cluster delivery and disputes, so the role carries real commercial weight. Key Responsibilities Technical negotiation with colocation providers Lead technical due diligence on candidate sites: power availability and energisation dates, redundancy topology, liquid-cooling capability, floor loading, rack logistics, fibre and meet-me access. Negotiate the technical schedules of the colocation agreement with commercial and legal: capacity and density commitments, power and cooling SLAs, temperature and flow envelopes, metering, expansion rights, change control and remedies. Challenge provider claims with evidence: single-line diagrams, P&IDs, load-bank and commissioning records, reference customers. Specification & SOW Work with cluster architects and OEMs (NVIDIA first) to capture rack, power, cooling, network and layout requirements, and keep them current across product generations. Write and own the technical SOW for white-space fitout: containment and cooling interfaces, power distribution to rack, structured cabling and pathways, rack and POD layout, security zoning, labelling and records. Define clear scope boundaries and responsibilities between us, the colocation provider, OEMs and installation contractors, with no gaps and no overlaps. Maintain a requirements baseline with traceability from OEM document, to SOW clause, to acceptance test. Design, installation & acceptance Review provider and contractor designs, shop drawings and method statements against the SOW; run design reviews and close findings. Define acceptance: factory and site tests, liquid flush and cleanliness, power quality, thermal performance at full load, fibre loss, burn-in, and the evidence pack needed for each gate. Attend key witness tests and sign off, or reject, completion of each phase before hardware is energised. Manage technical change requests and variations, and advise on cost and schedule impact. Knowledge & standards Build reusable reference designs, SOW templates and a site-scoring framework so each new deployment starts from a proven baseline. Track the roadmap: higher rack densities, 800 VDC distribution, new cooling classes and optics, and tell the business early what it means for sites already contracted. Deliverables You Own: Site technical assessment: Scored, evidence-based report per candidate site, comparable across providers, with risks and mitigations. Technical schedules to the colocation agreement: Measurable commitments, tested in acceptance, with remedies agreed by legal. Cluster white-space SOW: Complete enough that a contractor can price and build without asking us questions; traceable to OEM requirements. Reference designs and layouts: Rack, row and POD layouts, power and cooling single-line and P&ID level interfaces, fibre pathways and densities. Acceptance test plan and evidence pack: Pass and fail criteria set before work starts; signed results per gate. Requirements baseline and change log: One current version of the truth, with every variation recorded and costed. Risk and issues register: Technical risks to schedule and capacity, with owners and dates. Working Relationships: Cluster and network architects: You translate their cluster design into facility requirements, and they rely on you to say what a site can and cannot carry. OEMs, mainly NVIDIA: You are the facility-side counterpart; you obtain, interpret and challenge site-requirement documents. Colocation providers: Day-to-day technical counterpart through negotiation, build and acceptance. Procurement, legal and finance: You provide the technical substance of commercial terms and the impact of variations. Site operations and deployment teams: You hand over a clean specification and acceptance evidence, and take back lessons learned. What You Bring: 8 or more years in data centre design, delivery or technical consulting, including at least 3 years on high-density (50 kW per rack or more) or liquid-cooled deployments. Direct experience writing or reviewing technical specifications and SOWs for white-space fitout, and managing contractors against them to acceptance. Strong working knowledge of data centre power: MV and LV distribution, UPS and generator topologies, redundancy models (N+1, 2N, distributed), busway and rack power, metering and power quality. Strong working knowledge of cooling: direct-to-chip liquid cooling, CDUs, facility and technology loops, warm-water and dry-cooler designs, fluid quality and flushing, leak detection and containment. Working knowledge of structured cabling and pathways for large GPU fabrics (single-mode optics, high fibre counts, InfiniBand and Ethernet physical layers), and of rack and POD layouts. Familiarity with NVIDIA rack-scale platforms (GB200 or GB300 class, or later) and their facility requirements, and the ability to read OEM site-requirement documents critically. Proven ability to run technical negotiations with colocation or construction counterparties, and to explain trade-offs to commercial, legal and executive audiences. Command of standards such as EN 50600 and the Uptime Tier framework, ASHRAE TC 9.9 liquid-cooling guidance, and commissioning practice (levels 1 to 5). Excellent written communication: you produce clear, unambiguous contract-grade documents. Preferred Skills (Nice to Have): Experience at a hyperscaler, neocloud or colocation provider on the operator or customer side. Experience with 800 VDC or other DC distribution, large battery storage, or power smoothing for AI load swings. Chartered engineer status or equivalent; recognised data centre credentials (for example CDCP, CDFOM, Uptime ATD or AOS). Familiarity with BIM, digital-twin tools and requirements-management tools. Willingness to travel up to 30% to sites in the UK, Europe and the US. Success Measures: First 90 days: Audit current colocation contracts and SOWs and list technical gaps; publish a requirements baseline for the current NVIDIA platform; take over technical lead on one live negotiation; agree the site-scoring framework with the cluster architects. 6 months: One complete SOW issued and priced with no material scope disputes; acceptance plan agreed with the provider before build starts; reusable SOW template adopted by the team. 12 months: Every new site contracted on the template with traceable requirements; clusters accepted on schedule with no facility-caused performance issues; fewer late variations and a measurable cut in time from site shortlist to signed technical schedule. Qualities we look for: Set the standard: Every single day, you spot opportunities to constructively shake things up. Inspire the change: There’s no blueprint for the future. You’ll embrace challenges and change. You’re real and you’re true to yourself: We cherish and celebrate diversity so you’ll feel right at home whoever you are and whoever you’re talking to, you treat everyone the same. Get stuck in: You’d rather be building than overseeing. Our strategy will keep evolving, and so will you — attitude and adaptability matter more to us than a fixed playbook or a big team behind you. Package & Process: Employment type: Full-time, permanent. Travel: Up to 30%. Interview process: Talent Screening > Hiring Manager Screen > Technical Interview > Final with the Head of Data Centre Development. We are an equal opportunities employer and welcome applications from all backgrounds. Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

  • Negotiate the technical schedules of the colocation agreement with commercial and legal: capacity and density commitments, power and cooling SLAs, temperature and flow envelopes, metering, expansion rights, change control and remedies.

  • Challenge provider claims with evidence: single-line diagrams, P&IDs, load-bank and commissioning records, reference customers.

Specification & SOW

  • Work with cluster architects and OEMs (NVIDIA first) to capture rack, power, cooling, network and layout requirements, and keep them current across product generations.

  • Write and own the technical SOW for white-space fitout: containment and cooling interfaces, power distribution to rack, structured cabling and pathways, rack and POD layout, security zoning, labelling and records.

  • Define clear scope boundaries and responsibilities between us, the colocation provider, OEMs and installation contractors, with no gaps and no overlaps.

  • Maintain a requirements baseline with traceability from OEM document, to SOW clause, to acceptance test.

Design, installation & acceptance

  • Review provider and contractor designs, shop drawings and method statements against the SOW; run design reviews and close findings.

  • Define acceptance: factory and site tests, liquid flush and cleanliness, power quality, thermal performance at full load, fibre loss, burn-in, and the evidence pack needed for each gate.

  • Attend key witness tests and sign off, or reject, completion of each phase before hardware is energised.

  • Manage technical change requests and variations, and advise on cost and schedule impact.

Knowledge & standards

  • Build reusable reference designs, SOW templates and a site-scoring framework so each new deployment starts from a proven baseline.

  • Track the roadmap: higher rack densities, 800 VDC distribution, new cooling classes and optics, and tell the business early what it means for sites already contracted.

Deliverables You Own:

  • Site technical assessment: Scored, evidence-based report per candidate site, comparable across providers, with risks and mitigations.

  • Technical schedules to the colocation agreement: Measurable commitments, tested in acceptance, with remedies agreed by legal.

  • Cluster white-space SOW: Complete enough that a contractor can price and build without asking us questions; traceable to OEM requirements.

  • Reference designs and layouts: Rack, row and POD layouts, power and cooling single-line and P&ID level interfaces, fibre pathways and densities.

  • Acceptance test plan and evidence pack: Pass and fail criteria set before work starts; signed results per gate.

  • Requirements baseline and change log: One current version of the truth, with every variation recorded and costed.

  • Risk and issues register: Technical risks to schedule and capacity, with owners and dates.

Working Relationships:

  • Cluster and network architects: You translate their cluster design into facility requirements, and they rely on you to say what a site can and cannot carry.

  • OEMs, mainly NVIDIA: You are the facility-side counterpart; you obtain, interpret and challenge site-requirement documents.

  • Colocation providers: Day-to-day technical counterpart through negotiation, build and acceptance.

  • Procurement, legal and finance: You provide the technical substance of commercial terms and the impact of variations.

  • Site operations and deployment teams: You hand over a clean specification and acceptance evidence, and take back lessons learned.

What You Bring:

  • 8 or more years in data centre design, delivery or technical consulting, including at least 3 years on high-density (50 kW per rack or more) or liquid-cooled deployments.

  • Direct experience writing or reviewing technical specifications and SOWs for white-space fitout, and managing contractors against them to acceptance.

  • Strong working knowledge of data centre power: MV and LV distribution, UPS and generator topologies, redundancy models (N+1, 2N, distributed), busway and rack power, metering and power quality.

  • Strong working knowledge of cooling: direct-to-chip liquid cooling, CDUs, facility and technology loops, warm-water and dry-cooler designs, fluid quality and flushing, leak detection and containment.

  • Working knowledge of structured cabling and pathways for large GPU fabrics (single-mode optics, high fibre counts, InfiniBand and Ethernet physical layers), and of rack and POD layouts.

  • Familiarity with NVIDIA rack-scale platforms (GB200 or GB300 class, or later) and their facility requirements, and the ability to read OEM site-requirement documents critically.

  • Proven ability to run technical negotiations with colocation or construction counterparties, and to explain trade-offs to commercial, legal and executive audiences.

  • Command of standards such as EN 50600 and the Uptime Tier framework, ASHRAE TC 9.9 liquid-cooling guidance, and commissioning practice (levels 1 to 5).

  • Excellent written communication: you produce clear, unambiguous contract-grade documents.

Preferred Skills (Nice to Have):

  • Experience at a hyperscaler, neocloud or colocation provider on the operator or customer side.

  • Experience with 800 VDC or other DC distribution, large battery storage, or power smoothing for AI load swings.

  • Chartered engineer status or equivalent; recognised data centre credentials (for example CDCP, CDFOM, Uptime ATD or AOS).

  • Familiarity with BIM, digital-twin tools and requirements-management tools.

  • Willingness to travel up to 30% to sites in the UK, Europe and the US.

Success Measures:

  • 6 months: One complete SOW issued and priced with no material scope disputes; acceptance plan agreed with the provider before build starts; reusable SOW template adopted by the team.

title: Customer Operations Specialist - London
description: About Plasma Plasma is building the primary account for global money. Money used to belong to a country. Increasingly, it belongs to a person or business moving through many countries. People and businesses now earn, spend, save, hire and invest across borders. Traditional banks cannot serve this new world. Our first product, Plasma One, is a global money account: a place to receive, hold, send funds in seconds, earn yield and spend with a card in the local economy. Underneath is the Plasma network, built from first principles for stablecoin payments. Stablecoins make dollars faster, cheaper and more reliable to move. The opportunity is to become where all global money lands first: where income arrives, balances grow, payments move, businesses operate, and new financial products are built. The Team & Our Story We are a global team of founders, operators and engineers, obsessed with building the best products. We work at the cutting edge of financial innovation, using stablecoins to create tools for consumers and businesses. We operate with trust, clarity, and ambition: own your craft, move with urgency, contribute beyond your lane, back your teammates, debate rigorously, and keep raising the bar for what great means. Customer Experience Plasma is scaling its customer-facing operations across international markets, and we’re growing the Customer Experience Team to match. You’ll join an established team and take ownership of coverage for the CET time zone, making sure our customers get great support when they need it most. You’ll work across the full customer journey, from first contact through to resolution. Because we’re still building out our playbook, your input will directly shape the processes, standards, and team culture as we grow. You won’t just follow the process; you’ll help refine it. Some flexibility in working hours & weekend shifts will be needed to support coverage and the occasional busy period. We’re looking for a hard-working self-starter who thrives in a fast-moving startup environment and is committed to the mission alongside the rest of the team. The role Own the customer experience day-to-day: Be the first person our customers reach when something goes wrong or they need help. You will handle inbound queries across chat, email, and support tooling, and take accountability for the quality and speed of every response. Be the right hand of the Ops lead: Work directly alongside the Head of Operations to build out processes, identify gaps, and support decisions as we scale the team internationally. This is not a back-office support role. You will be involved in how we think about operations. Build the foundations: We are early. Many of the processes, templates, and escalation paths do not exist yet. You will create them. From response frameworks to internal guides, you will help lay the groundwork the team will rely on as we grow. Support international team scaling: As we hire Ops team members in new markets, you will help onboard them, share knowledge, and maintain consistency in how we deliver for customers across regions. Spot problems before they become patterns: Track issues across the customer base, flag recurring themes to Product and Engineering, and help prioritise fixes that actually move the needle for customers. Work across teams: Collaborate with Compliance, KYC, and Product to make sure the customer experience is joined up, especially during onboarding and verification flows where things can go wrong quickly. Represent the customer internally: Your proximity to customer feedback is valuable. Use it. Bring customer insight into internal conversations and push for improvements that matter. Be Flexible with Shift Rotation: Most weeks you’ll work the normal Mon-Fri, however team members currently rotate weekend shifts which means that you may be required to work a weekend shift once every 6 weeks. You’ll then be able to take those days worked off the following week. The Bar 1 to 3 years of experience in customer operations, customer success, or a support role, ideally within fintech, payments, or crypto. We will consider strong candidates from outside these sectors if the fit is right. Someone who takes ownership. You do not wait to be told. When something is broken or missing, you fix it or flag it. You hold yourself to a high standard even when no one is watching. Clear and direct in how you communicate. You can write a helpful, professional response under pressure and explain a complex situation simply. You know the difference between being thorough and overcomplicating things. Competent English Language - our team communicates in english so being competent with the language is a requirement. Comfortable with ambiguity. This is an early-stage company. About Plasma

Plasma is building the primary account for global money.

Money used to belong to a country. Increasingly, it belongs to a person or business moving through many countries. People and businesses now earn, spend, save, hire and invest across borders. Traditional banks cannot serve this new world.

Our first product, Plasma One, is a global money account: a place to receive, hold, send funds in seconds, earn yield and spend with a card in the local economy.

Underneath is the Plasma network, built from first principles for stablecoin payments. Stablecoins make dollars faster, cheaper and more reliable to move.

The opportunity is to become where all global money lands first: where income arrives, balances grow, payments move, businesses operate, and new financial products are built.


The Team & Our Story

We are a global team of founders, operators and engineers, obsessed with building the best products. We work at the cutting edge of financial innovation, using stablecoins to create tools for consumers and businesses.

Customer Experience

Plasma is scaling its customer-facing operations across international markets, and we’re growing the Customer Experience Team to match. You’ll join an established team and take ownership of coverage for the CET time zone, making sure our customers get great support when they need it most.

description: <div class="content-intro"><h2 class="job-details__description-header text-color-secondary font-family-secondary" data-bind="i18n: 'job-details.employer-description-title'">About Us</h2> <div class="job-details__description-content basic-formatter" data-bind="html: pageData().job.corporateDescription"> <div>Fanatics is building a leading global digital sports platform. We ignite the passions of global sports fans and maximize the presence and reach for our hundreds of sports partners globally by offering products and services across Fanatics Commerce, Fanatics Collectibles, and Fanatics Betting &amp; Gaming, allowing sports fans to Buy, Collect, and Bet. Through the Fanatics platform, sports fans can buy licensed fan gear, jerseys, lifestyle and streetwear products, headwear, and hardgoods; collect physical and digital trading cards, sports memorabilia, and other digital assets; and bet as the company builds its Sportsbook and iGaming platform. Fanatics has an established database of over 100 million global sports fans; a global partner network with approximately 900 sports properties, including major national and international professional sports leagues, players associations, teams, colleges, college conferences and retail partners, 2,500 athletes and celebrities, and 200 exclusive athletes; and over 2,000 retail locations, including its Lids retail stores. Our more than 22,000 employees are committed to relentlessly enhancing the fan experience and delighting sports fans globally.&nbsp;</div> </div> <p>&nbsp;</p></div><p><strong>Primary Focus:</strong></p> <p>As Director, Performance Creative Strategy at Fanatics Betting &amp; Gaming (FBG), you are responsible for defining the strategic priorities, audience opportunities and learning agenda that shape Fanatics Casino performance creative. Complaints are where things get real - the customer is already frustrated or in distress, the stakes are higher, and poor handling has direct regulatory consequences.

What you’ll do

  • Own our security posture. You’ll be the person accountable for security at GetGround. Assess where we are today and define a roadmap that balances security with what the business needs.   • Stay ahead of threats. The threat landscape is moving faster than ever, and AI is driving much of that change. AI-generated phishing, deepfake social engineering, prompt injection and data leaking through AI tools are all part of it.   • Run our SIEM and own our alerts. Make sure logs from GCP, identity, endpoints, SaaS tools and our own platform reach the SIEM and stay there. Write detection rules, map coverage against MITRE ATT&CK, tune out the noise and make sure nothing important goes unnoticed.

  • Automate response. Build playbooks that contain common threats as soon as an alert fires. Lead incident response when things go wrong, and make sure we learn from it.

  • Protect the data we hold. Know where sensitive data lives, who can access it and when it moves. Secure every channel it passes through: devices through endpoint detection and response (EDR) and anti-malware monitoring and protection, email and cloud storage through data loss prevention, and our platform and tools through access controls. Make the secure path the easy path for everyone at GetGround.

  • Work across the business. Partner with our site reliability engineer and product engineers on secure infrastructure and design, and with Compliance on our obligations. Assess vendors and run training people actually remember.

  • Set our policies and back them with working controls. Build and keep updating our security policies, best practices and information security management system (ISMS). Implement and automate the technical controls behind our security certifications and frameworks, such as ISO 27001, so that passing an audit reflects how we really operate.

  • Hands-on detection and response experience. You’ve run a SIEM, built detection rules and owned alerting in production. You know what a bad log looks like.

title: Technical Product Manager
description: About Kernel Agents are starting to sell, buy and operate on behalf of companies. But before an agent can close a deal, qualify an account, route a lead or assess risk, it has to answer a basic question: which company is this? Today, that answer is messy, and no one answers it reliably. Business identity lives across CRMs, ERPs and third-party datasets full of duplicates, missing parent companies, stale addresses and incorrect enrichment. The cost shows up across the enterprise: sales teams miss revenue opportunities because they lack the right account context; operations teams take on avoidable exposure because risk signals are fragmented or wrong; and finance teams end up chasing, writing off, or defaulting on bad debt that should have been caught earlier. Humans have worked around that mess for years. Agents cannot. They need a reliable business identity layer they can trust. Kernel is building that layer: the business registry for agents. We issue a permanent Kernel ID for every business, plus the context an agent needs to act on it. We have strong product-market fit: Ops, data, and revenue teams at Gong, Legora, Mistral, Canva, and Checkout already use Kernel across their enterprise systems. Agents are next, and there will be far more of them. We have raised $20M from top VCs and operators, and we are growing 12x YoY . The role You will own one of Kernel’s product areas end-to-end, working directly with the founders and the engineering team Own all stages from discovery to implementation for our core product areas and bets Data- and metrics-driven (without being obstinate about it) Tolerate (maybe even relish) ambiguity, and know when to make decisions quickly vs. when something needs more thought Bridge the link between our customers and our engineering team Help shape the product roadmap and vision for Kernel What we’re looking for We are looking for a full-stack product thinker who can own and lead product work from discovery to implementation. Scar tissue : 6+ years of Product Management experience in an early-stage environment, where you’ve learned the hard way what works and what doesn’t, and built complex products and features along the way Evals: Comfortable with evals for agents and driving quality improvements via evals and recursive self-improvement Technical IQ : Comfortable with API, data pipelines, SQL, and so on. A background in product engineering is a strong plus. Extreme ownership : You own your area, cradle-to-grave; this is not a relay race where you only do one part and then hand off the next bit of product work to someone else Clever use of AI : You’re an aggressive and proficient user of AI, but you never switch off the local LLM that you were born with :) ⚠️ This role may not be for you if you Want to work remotely. Business identity lives across CRMs, ERPs and third-party datasets full of duplicates, missing parent companies, stale addresses and incorrect enrichment.   • Build the quality, documentation, and regulatory groundwork (design history, ISO 13485-style discipline, CE/UKCA pathway) appropriate to a research-device product

  • Contribute to the industrialisation of our rodent recording platform where the manufacturing and OTA problems overlap

  • Min 3+ years (ideal 7+) in hardware product management, product engineering, or programme management, with several products you personally took from prototype to volume manufacture

  • Direct, demonstrable experience with contract manufacturers: you have run RFQs, sat through NPI builds, argued about yield, and fixed a production line problem from 6,000 miles away

  • Deep understanding of connected-device architecture: OTA update mechanisms, device provisioning, telemetry, fleet management, and what it costs to get these wrong

  • Background in neuroscience, biomedical engineering, or a related field

  • Experience with multi-sensor time synchronisation and the data infrastructure behind it

What we offer

title: General Counsel at amo
description: amo is a Paris-based consumer social company. We want to build Europe's most ambitious consumer company. Our apps Bump and Sugar are used by millions of people all over the globe. Location sits at the heart of one of our current products, and privacy, trust and safety are part of how we build, not an afterthought. We're scaling fast, and this comes with legal implications. We want them handled in a way that speeds the business up. The role: We're hiring our first General Counsel to own amo's legal function end to end. This is a business role, not a support function: you'll work directly with the cofounders, join discussions from the start and work with every team, from Product and Distribution to People, Engineering and Finance. You'll draft, negotiate and advise yourself on the topics that matter most. For everything else, you'll build and run a network of local counsel, with the right firm for each topic and each market, and turn their advice into clear decisions for the team. How we think about legal: At amo, legal starts from the product, to serve our users. We're not looking for someone who applies the rules by the book, but for someone who understands what we're building and why, and finds the legal approach that makes sense for it. You'll be judged on what you enable, not on how many memos you write. Product and users first: you join discussions early and work with the team toward the same goal: making projects to life, fast and safe. Pragmatic on risk: you know which rules are non-negotiable, where there is room for judgement, and how much risk is worth taking for the business. You give a recommendation, not a list of risks. Built for scale: you set up the contracts, policies and processes that enable our growth. What you'll own: You'll cover every legal question that comes with scaling a consumer app across markets, working with the right local counsel on each topic: Corporate: general corporate, group structure as we expand internationally, BSPCE plans and employee liquidity operations. Employment: French labour law across the employee lifecycle, from contracts, immigration and internal rules to terminations. Trademarks and IP: our global trademark portfolio: filing strategy, oppositions, watch services and disputes. Patents and content licensing as they come. Compliance and data protection: GDPR, protection of minors, DSA, app store policies, and more. Regulator and law enforcement requests. Commercial contracts: vendors and SaaS, partnerships, creator and influencer agreements, advertising, data processing agreements. Templates and a self-serve process so teams can move autonomously. Litigation: pre-litigation and litigation across jurisdictions, with outside counsel. Clear risk assessments and options for the cofounders. M&A: acquisitions and strategic transactions when the time comes, including due diligence, structuring and integration. What success looks like: Teams ship features, sign deals and expand without waiting on legal. The cofounders spend far less time on legal: topics get tracked, briefed and closed without one of them driving each one, and nothing is discovered late. The right local counsel is in place for each topic and market, on a budget we control. What we're looking for: Startup and scaleup experience, at our stage and beyond. 7+ years of legal experience, including a senior in-house role (General Counsel, Deputy GC or Head of Legal) at a tech company. You've lived the stage we're at international expansion, fast growth. Expert in French and EU law. French legal training, with deep knowledge of French corporate and employment law, GDPR and EU digital regulation. Admission to the bar (CAPA) is a plus. Global outlook. You've handled matters in several jurisdictions and know how to find, brief and challenge the right local counsel for each topic and market. A true generalist. You move from a vendor contract negotiation to a trademark opposition in the same day, and know when to go deep yourself and when to bring in a specialist. Product and business first. You adapt the legal approach to what the product and the business need, and give clear recommendations in plain language. You help the team move fast without taking blind risks. Hands-on. You draft and negotiate yourself and don't need a team to get things done. Fluent in French and English. Comfortable with little structure. You set your own priorities in a noisy environment and would rather be judged on what you enabled than on how busy you were. Discretion. You handle sensitive matters, including disputes, with complete confidentiality. Nice to have: Experience at a consumer app, social or gaming company. Hands-on work with GDPR, content moderation (DSA). M&A transactions led or closed, buy side or sell side. A few years at a top-tier law firm before going in-house. Exposure to a crisis, whether regulatory, press or security. Why join: You'll build the function from the ground up, with a seat next to the cofounders on the decisions that shape the company and a direct impact on the trajectory of a company that serves users all over the globe. raw.description:
- About Quandela:

Quandela is a European deeptech scale-up developing modular, scalable and energy-efficient photonic and spin-optical quantum computers, accessible through the cloud and on-premises.

With over 140 employees, we develop our own hardware and software stack, from semiconductor quantum emitters and photonic processors to quantum control systems and algorithms.

Our ambition is to build large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computers, combining quantum dot technologies, scalable spin-photon interfaces and distributed entanglement within future Spin-Optical Quantum Computing (SPOQC) architectures.

- About this position:

You will join Quandela's Semiconductor Optics Team, bringing together expertise in quantum optics, spin physics, semiconductor technologies and quantum information.

Your focus will be to develop and validate photon-mediated spin-spin entanglement protocols, improve spin coherence and operation fidelity, and advance optical control techniques for future hybrid quantum computing architectures.

We are looking for an experienced experimental scientist who can independently drive complex experimental activities, shape technical directions and translate scientific results into reliable technological building blocks, working closely with our research and engineering teams.

With several experimental building blocks still under development, you'll have room to shape technical choices, tackle open scientific challenges and directly influence our technology roadmap.

- What you'll do:

Spin-based quantum experiments

  • Design, develop and optimize optical experiments involving spin-photon sources.
  • Implement optical control schemes for spin initialization, readout and manipulation.
  • Characterize spin coherence, operation fidelity and entanglement quality.

Scientific and experimental ownership

  • Independently drive experimental investigations, from design to validation.
  • Structure and prioritize scientific activities, milestones and technical challenges.
  • Troubleshoot complex experimental systems and propose technical improvements.
  • Share expertise and support less experienced colleagues when relevant.

Technology development and integration

  • Develop and validate photon-mediated spin-spin entanglement protocols.
  • Collaborate with theory, electronics and semiconductor technology teams.
  • Improve experimental robustness, reproducibility and system performance.
  • Translate scientific results into demonstrators and technological building blocks for future multi-spin architectures.

- How You Will Grow:

During your first 3 months 
You will become familiar with Quandela's experimental platforms and ongoing demonstrators, contributing your expertise to current technical challenges.

Within 6 months 
You will drive dedicated experimental workstreams, contribute to key technical decisions and strengthen theory-to-experiment feedback loops.

Within 1 year 
You will help shape the team's experimental direction, advance distributed entanglement demonstrations and contribute to future spin-based architectures.

Requirements

- What we're looking for

We are looking for an experienced experimental researcher combining strong scientific expertise, technical autonomy and the ability to drive complex research activities.

Must-have

  • PhD in Spin Physics, Quantum Optics or a related field.
  • Hands-on experience with spin-based quantum systems (control, readout or coherence measurements).
  • Proven autonomy in designing, optimizing and troubleshooting complex quantum experiments.
  • Strong understanding of quantum optics, spin coherence and experimental measurement techniques.
  • Ability to lead scientific activities and make independent technical decisions.
  • Comfortable collaborating across experimental, theory and engineering teams

Important, but you can grow here

  • Photon-mediated entanglement protocols and multi-spin architectures.
  • Semiconductor quantum emitters, quantum dots and spin-photon interfaces.
  • Advanced optical control, cryogenic platforms and fast electronics.
  • Experimental qualification, system integration and technology transfer.

Bonus points

  • Experience bridging academic research and industrial R&D.
  • Experience coordinating scientific projects or mentoring researchers.

- Career Stage & Team Contribution: 

We primarily target candidates with a PhD and 4+ years of postdoctoral or equivalent R&D experience, combining scientific expertise with strong experimental autonomy.

Researchers completing a substantial postdoc are also welcome if they demonstrate scientific maturity, technical ownership and readiness for broader responsibilities.

People management experience is not required. What matters is your ability to drive scientific activities, tackle complex technical challenges and share your expertise with the team.

Benefits

  • Profit-sharing and a company savings plan. 
  • Public transport subscription covered at 50%. 
  • Annual sustainable mobility bonus for eco-friendly transport (e-bike, electric car). 
  • Fully covered health insurance (Alan). 
  • Referral program (€1,000 for a junior and €2,000 for an experienced candidate). 
  • Access to a nursery via choisir-ma-creche or contribution to childcare expenses. 
  • Subsidy for gym membership and sports activities (Gymlib). 
  • Meal subsidies (Swile). 

 Localisation of the position : Based at the IPVF campus in Palaiseau, within the Paris-Saclay research ecosystem. 

Process: 

  • Talent Acquisition Interview (30–45 min)
  • Hiring Manager Interview (45–60 min)
  • Technical discussion and presentation of previous research work
  • Meeting with the team and scientific discussion
  • Reference checks
  • Offer

- Beyond That

At Quandela, you'll work on challenging scientific questions while helping turn experimental advances into technologies for future quantum computers.

Our spin-based platforms are still evolving, leaving room to explore new approaches, influence technical directions and take real ownership of experimental challenges.

If you're excited by the idea of combining ambitious quantum research with tangible technological impact, we'd love to hear from you, even if your background doesn't match every requirement.

title: GPU Engineer
description: About Kog At Kog, we're building real-time LLM inference for AI agents. Coding agents execute sequences of tasks where each step depends on the model's previous response. The faster the model generates tokens, the faster these agents can reason, code, and act. Our approach is to co-design model architecture, the inference engine, and low-level GPU kernels to minimize generation latency on standard NVIDIA and AMD datacenter GPUs. We've developed several technologies to make this possible: Monokernel: a persistent GPU program that keeps the entire token generation loop on the GPU, avoiding CPU handoffs. KCCL: our custom inter-GPU communication layer, designed to minimize latency. Delayed Tensor Parallelism (DTP): a model architecture that overlaps communication with computation and weight loading. Laneformer 2B: our code-generation model demonstrating this co-design approach. Our engineers work directly with GPU hardware, using CUDA, PTX, HIP, and CDNA ISA to optimize execution. Implementing and optimizing a new AI model for a specific GPU architecture can take months of manual engineering. Meanwhile, new models are constantly being released. Our goal is to use AI agents to implement and optimize the models we choose on the GPUs we choose, in a fraction of the time required today. These agents will build on the GPU optimizations and hardware insights our team has developed. They'll explore optimization strategies, generate and modify kernels, verify correctness, benchmark performance on real hardware, and iterate based on the results. We want to make model porting and GPU optimization much faster and repeatable, allowing Kog to keep pace with the latest AI models rather than spending months adapting each one manually. This is a major engineering direction we're now developing, and you'll help shape it. Learn more at https://blog.kog.ai . What you'll work on You'll join our GPU engineering team to tackle challenging performance problems and help build the internal agents that will accelerate this work. About Kog

At Kog, we're building real-time LLM inference for AI agents.

Coding agents execute sequences of tasks where each step depends on the model's previous response. The faster the model generates tokens, the faster these agents can reason, code, and act.

Our approach is to co-design model architecture, the inference engine, and low-level GPU kernels to minimize generation latency on standard NVIDIA and AMD datacenter GPUs.

We've developed several technologies to make this possible:

  • Monokernel: a persistent GPU program that keeps the entire token generation loop on the GPU, avoiding CPU handoffs.

  • KCCL: our custom inter-GPU communication layer, designed to minimize latency.

  • Delayed Tensor Parallelism (DTP): a model architecture that overlaps communication with computation and weight loading.

  • Laneformer 2B: our code-generation model demonstrating this co-design approach.

Our engineers work directly with GPU hardware, using CUDA, PTX, HIP, and CDNA ISA to optimize execution.

Implementing and optimizing a new AI model for a specific GPU architecture can take months of manual engineering. Meanwhile, new models are constantly being released.

Our goal is to use AI agents to implement and optimize the models we choose on the GPUs we choose, in a fraction of the time required today.

These agents will build on the GPU optimizations and hardware insights our team has developed. They'll explore optimization strategies, generate and modify kernels, verify correctness, benchmark performance on real hardware, and iterate based on the results.

We want to make model porting and GPU optimization much faster and repeatable, allowing Kog to keep pace with the latest AI models rather than spending months adapting each one manually.

This is a major engineering direction we're now developing, and you'll help shape it.

Learn more at https://blog.kog.ai.

What you'll work on

You'll join our GPU engineering team to tackle challenging performance problems and help build the internal agents that will accelerate this work.

  • Develop and optimize GPU kernels using C++, CUDA, HIP, and low-level instructions.

  • Investigate GPU architecture, memory access, synchronization, and execution bottlenecks.

  • Profile and benchmark workloads to identify and validate performance improvements.

  • Optimize inference operations and communication across multiple GPUs.

  • Implement and optimize new AI models on NVIDIA and AMD GPUs.

  • Help build AI agents for GPU engineering, enabling automated code optimization, correctness testing, benchmarking, and iterative improvements.

  • Take ownership of technical decisions and their implementation.

What we're looking for

We're looking for an experienced GPU Engineer who can contribute quickly and independently to complex performance problems.

  • Strong hands-on experience developing and optimizing GPU kernels, ideally using CUDA C++ or HIP/ROCm.

  • Deep understanding of GPU architecture, memory hierarchy, parallel execution, and performance bottlenecks.

  • Strong C++ skills and experience profiling and benchmarking GPU workloads.

  • Proven ownership of challenging technical projects, from implementation to measured results.

  • Interest in developing AI agents and tools to accelerate GPU engineering.

Experience with PTX, CDNA ISA, multi-GPU systems, low-latency inference, or GPU performance portability is particularly valuable.

A PhD in HPC, computer science, or a related field is a plus when backed by substantial engineering work. Previous experience building AI agents is not required.

Location and availability

Candidates must already be based in Paris or elsewhere in Île-de-France.

We are not considering relocation from other regions or countries for this position.

We're looking for someone who can join the team quickly.

We are looking for a CFD Workflow Automation Intern for a 6-month internship in Toulouse. The role will focus on developing robust, reusable workflows for meshing, simulation setup and launching, data extraction, post-processing, and standardized reporting, with particular emphasis on Cadence and Ansys Fluent environments. The internship is intended to reduce manual effort, improve repeatability, and shorten analysis turnaround time across the Fluidics Department. The intern will work with engineers from both teams to identify high-value automation opportunities, translate existing engineering practices into scripts and workflows, and validate the resulting tools on representative analysis cases. Prior expertise in Cadence or Ansys Fluent is not required; strong programming ability and a willingness to learn the relevant engineering applications are more important. Key Responsibilities: • Develop scripts and utilities to automate CFD meshing, simulation setup, job launching, monitoring, and post-processing activities. • Automate recurring workflows in Cadence and Ansys Fluent, using the scripting and interface capabilities available within those environments. • Create reusable tools for data extraction, visualization, comparison, and standardized reporting of CFD results. • Work with the Turbomachinery Fluidic Design Team to streamline the design-analysis iteration loop, including comparison of CFD results with design intent. • Work with the Fluidic Analysis Team to identify repetitive analysis tasks and convert them into reliable, maintainable automated processes. • Define input requirements, verification checks, error handling, and user documentation so that the developed tools can be adopted by different engineers. • Validate automated workflows against existing manual processes and document accuracy, repeatability, limitations, and expected time savings. • Present progress and results to the participating teams and incorporate user feedback into successive tool improvements. What you need to be successful: • Final-year student or recent graduate in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related technical field. • Strong programming skills, preferably in Python; experience with additional scripting languages is an advantage. • Understanding of software development fundamentals, including modular code, version control, testing, debugging, and documentation. • Ability to analyse an existing manual workflow, identify repetitive steps, and translate the process into a structured automation solution. • Interest in CFD, numerical simulation, engineering data processing, or scientific computing. Previous application-specific experience is not mandatory. • Fluency in written and spoken English. Soft Skills: • Analytical and methodical approach to problem solving. • Proactive mindset and willingness to take ownership of a defined work package. • Clear communication and ability to gather requirements from engineers in different teams. • Attention to detail, with a focus on reliability, traceability, and usability. • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively in a multicultural, multidisciplinary environment. Other useful skills: • Experience with engineering or scientific Python and Matlab libraries for data processing and visualization. • Familiarity with Linux, command-line tools, batch processing, high-performance computing, or job schedulers. • Exposure to APIs, graphical user interfaces, dashboards, or automated report generation. • Familiarity with Git or another version-control system. • Previous exposure to Cadence, Ansys Fluent, CFD meshing, or simulation postprocessing is beneficial but not required. • Basic knowledge of fluid dynamics or numerical methods is an advantage. Supervision and collaboration: The intern will be supervised by a designated engineer and will collaborate with representatives of both the Turbomachinery Fluidic Design Team and the Fluidic Analysis Team. The assignment will be managed as a shared departmental initiative, with priorities defined according to the automation needs and potential impact identified by the participating teams. So, if you're enthusiastic about this role but your prior experience doesn't align perfectly with every qualification mentioned in the job description, we still strongly encourage you to apply. You might just be the ideal candidate for this position or other opportunities within our organization. Pangea Propulsion is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion. We consider all applications without discrimination on any legally protected grounds. We welcome applications from persons with disabilities and we can provide reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process and in the workplace. About Pangea Propulsion: We are a company dedicated to developing advanced propulsion systems for the space industry based on three key principles: high efficiency, sustainability, and reusability. We are revolutionizing the space industry with ground-breaking innovations that allow us to offer the best performance to cost propulsion systems.

Our goal is to be the propulsion provider for the next generation of spacecraft, which is essential to meet demands and compete in the booming space market of the next decade. We are a passionate, multicultural, and multidisciplinary team pushing the boundaries of what is possible in space propulsion technology. We have already made history by successfully testing the world's first 3D-printed Methalox Aerospike engine, marking a significant milestone for the space industry. We are looking for talented professionals to join our international teams in Barcelona and Toulouse.

We want to be a key player in improving diversity in the Aerospace sector as, in Pangea, we believe that diversity (gender, age, race, sexual orientation, beliefs, disability, culture, etc.) is a key to success. Within Pangea, everyone can grow with the same opportunities. We encourage you to apply. Individually we are different, but together we are an amazing team!

We are looking for a CFD Workflow Automation Intern for a 6-month internship in Toulouse.

About the role:

We are seeking a highly skilled intern with a strong programming background and an interest in engineering simulation to help automate repetitive CFD activities across the Turbomachinery Fluidic Design Team and the Fluidic Analysis Team.

The role will focus on developing robust, reusable workflows for meshing, simulation setup and launching, data extraction, post-processing, and standardized reporting, with particular emphasis on Cadence and Ansys Fluent environments. The internship is intended to reduce manual effort, improve repeatability, and shorten analysis turnaround time across the Fluidics Department.

The intern will work with engineers from both teams to identify high-value automation opportunities, translate existing engineering practices into scripts and workflows, and validate the resulting tools on representative analysis cases. Prior expertise in Cadence or Ansys Fluent is not required; strong programming ability and a willingness to learn the relevant engineering applications are more important.

Key Responsibilities:

• Develop scripts and utilities to automate CFD meshing, simulation setup, job launching, monitoring, and post-processing activities.

• Automate recurring workflows in Cadence and Ansys Fluent, using the scripting and interface capabilities available within those environments.

• Create reusable tools for data extraction, visualization, comparison, and standardized reporting of CFD results. • Work with the Turbomachinery Fluidic Design Team to streamline the design-analysis iteration loop, including comparison of CFD results with design intent.

• Work with the Fluidic Analysis Team to identify repetitive analysis tasks and convert them into reliable, maintainable automated processes.

• Define input requirements, verification checks, error handling, and user documentation so that the developed tools can be adopted by different engineers.

• Validate automated workflows against existing manual processes and document accuracy, repeatability, limitations, and expected time savings.

• Present progress and results to the participating teams and incorporate user feedback into successive tool improvements.

• Strong programming skills, preferably in Python; experience with additional scripting languages is an advantage.

• Understanding of software development fundamentals, including modular code, version control, testing, debugging, and documentation.

• Ability to analyse an existing manual workflow, identify repetitive steps, and translate the process into a structured automation solution.

• Interest in CFD, numerical simulation, engineering data processing, or scientific computing. Previous application-specific experience is not mandatory.

• Fluency in written and spoken English.

Soft Skills:

• Analytical and methodical approach to problem solving.

• Proactive mindset and willingness to take ownership of a defined work package.

• Clear communication and ability to gather requirements from engineers in different teams.

• Attention to detail, with a focus on reliability, traceability, and usability.

• Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively in a multicultural, multidisciplinary environment.

• Familiarity with Linux, command-line tools, batch processing, high-performance computing, or job schedulers.

• Exposure to APIs, graphical user interfaces, dashboards, or automated report generation.

• Familiarity with Git or another version-control system.

Tasks Trade Shows & Events Plan and coordinate Goodweek’s participation in international trade shows and industry events. Manage all event logistics and visual branding, including booth design, signage, branded merchandise, localized brochures, interactive activities, and contests. Localisation, Multilingual Adaptation & Content Rollout Manage the localization and adaptation of marketing materials across Goodweek’s target markets. Develop scalable processes to roll out localized content efficiently, using multilingual templates and automated asset creation where possible. Ensure brand consistency and maintain high-quality standards across all translated and adapted content before publication. Digital Acquisition & Budget Management Develop and execute paid acquisition campaigns for each target market using LinkedIn Campaign Manager. Manage the overall acquisition budget and continuously optimize cost per lead (CPL) and marketing-qualified lead (MQL) generation across regions. Represent the partner marketing perspective in program design, working with Rev team, Operations, and Legal on how benefits, MDF, and tier criteria will work in practice. Build joint marketing plan templates for reseller partners, including campaign calendars and success metrics. Run Distributor-led acquisition campaigns using co-branded and localized kits for each market, and help Distributors customize them for their own MSP clients. Define KPIs, track campaign ROI, and prepare monthly performance reports and dashboards. Create, optimise, and A/B test localized landing pages and conversion forms to improve campaign performance. Marketing Automation & Workflow Optimisation Create automated lead follow-ups, including multilingual emails within 48 hours after events. Scale global communication workflows and develop modular email templates that can be adapted across markets. Automate repetitive marketing tasks and improve the efficiency of campaign execution. Brand, Design & Content Production Create visual assets for the business, including advertising banners, infographics, print materials, and event signage. Support organic LinkedIn growth by developing engaging post formats, carousels, key takeaways, and live event coverage. Create and coordinate high-value marketing content, including customer case studies, blog articles, and lead-generation materials such as use cases and customer testimonials. Requirements Proficiency in English and either Spanish or French. 3–5 years of experience in digital marketing or communications, ideally with initial experience in an international environment. Advanced experience in design tools such as Canva. Hands-on experience managing paid campaigns across multiple countries, particularly LinkedIn Ads, and working with marketing automation platforms. Strong organizational skills and a structured approach to managing multilingual marketing assets across different markets. Ability to work effectively in a dynamic environment, adapt quickly, and reprioritize when needed. Strong sense of ownership, initiative, and a hands-on approach to execution. Genuine enthusiasm for meeting and engaging with international prospects and partners at trade shows and industry events. title: Manager Architect Cloud - Paris
description: <p><strong>Présentation du poste :</strong></p> <p>Concevoir une architecture d’IA, c’est engager une entreprise pour plusieurs années : l’emplacement des données, la gestion des accès, la manière dont un agent passe en production sous le regard des équipes de sécurité. Ces choix structurants, vous les construisez avec nos clients.</p> <p>Tout le reste, ce sont les ambitions fonctionnelles et techniques du client, son cadre réglementaire, son budget, les compétences qu'il peut réellement mobiliser en interne, la gouvernance qu'il veut installer, et un écosystème d'éditeurs qui gravite autour de lui. Votre rôle est de trouver le point d'équilibre entre ces forces, de le faire accepter, puis de le réajuster dès que l'une d'elles bouge.</p> <p>Votre point de départ n’est pas la technologie, mais l’ambition métier. Vous la traduisez en une plateforme data ou agentique pensée pour s’intégrer au système d’information existant, avec son histoire, ses contraintes et ses équipes. Votre rôle ne s’arrête pas à la validation du schéma cible : vous accompagnez les équipes de delivery jusqu’à la mise en production.</p> <p>À titre d’exemple, chez l’un de nos clients, chaque nouvel agent repose désormais sur une plateforme commune qui gère nativement les droits d’accès, le monitoring et les coûts. Chaque cas d’usage s’appuie ainsi sur les fondations posées pour les précédents.</p> <p>Ce poste s’adresse à vous si vous aimez embrasser un système dans son ensemble, prendre les décisions qui engagent et en expliquer les raisons.</p> <p>Artefact est le partenaire de confiance des plus grandes entreprises mondiales pour déployer l’IA : 3 000 AI makers dans plus de 30 pays, plus de 1 000 clients. En France, vous rejoignez le département Engineering (environ 300 personnes, sous la responsabilité du CTO), au sein du chapter AI Architect.</p> <p><strong>Activités et responsabilités :</strong></p> <p>Sur un projet, vous travaillez en étroite collaboration avec les AI Applied Engineers, qui construisent et font tourner ce que vous concevez, et avec les AI Product Managers, qui portent le produit avec le client.</p> <p>Côté client, deux publics sont à convaincre : les directions métier, avec lesquelles vous définissez la cible, et les équipes IT, sécurité, réseau et exploitation, sans l’adhésion desquelles rien ne passe en production. Une architecture qu’elles n’ont pas validée ne dépasse pas le stade du document. Vous êtes aussi l'interlocuteur des achats, de la conformité et des éditeurs qui veulent se positionner.</p> <p>Au sein du chapter, vous relisez les designs de vos pairs, contribuez à faire grandir les architectes et les profils d’ingénierie qui vous entourent, et mettez en commun ce qui fonctionne. Vous travaillez également avec nos partenaires technologiques et les autres équipes d’Artefact.</p> <p><strong>Vos responsabilités :</strong></p> <ul> <li>Traduire les objectifs, les contraintes et les délais du client en une architecture que le métier comme l’IT comprennent, et défendre vos choix devant eux.</li> <li>Concevoir des plateformes data et agentiques, on premise, dans le cloud ou en hybride.</li> <li>Découper les périmètres techniques en fonction de la façon dont les équipes du client sont organisées.</li> <li>Arbitrer entre les options en pesant leur valeur métier, leur coût total, leur conformité, leur dépendance à un éditeur et la capacité du client à les faire vivre.</li> <li>Aider le client à évaluer et à mettre en concurrence des éditeurs, sans parti pris.</li> <li>Préparer les propositions commerciales : cadrer la solution, la chiffrer et construire la roadmap de delivery.</li> <li>Tenir la ligne&nbsp; pendant le delivery : relire les designs, trancher les arbitrages et réajuster la cible quand le contexte du client change.</li> <li>Faire vivre les patterns de référence et les bonnes pratiques du chapter, et suivre de près les évolutions de l’IA, du cloud et de la data.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Profil recherché :</strong></p> <p>Nous recherchons une personne qui pense comme un consultant et raisonne comme un ingénieur. Les architectes qui réussissent chez nous sont, entre autres, des profils techniques passés par le conseil, des pre-sales engineers, des FDEs, ou des personnes avec une expérience en tant que CTO.</p> <p><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Les indispensables :</span></p> <ol> <li>Vous avez conçu une architecture data ou IA qui a été mise en production, et vous savez expliquer pourquoi vous avez écarté les autres options, techniques ou non.</li> <li>Vous avez déjà recommandé une option techniquement moins séduisante parce qu'elle correspondait mieux au budget, aux compétences, à la gouvernance ou à la réglementation du client.</li> <li>Vous maîtrisez au moins un grand cloud (Google Cloud, Azure ou AWS) ainsi que les fondamentaux de la sécurité et du réseau : IAM, gestion des secrets, architecture réseau.</li> <li>Vous avez rédigé des dossiers d’architecture (HLD et LLD) qui ont servi de base à une équipe de delivery.</li> <li>Vous avez codé pendant une partie significative de votre parcours. Aujourd'hui, vous savez lire du code, challenger un design et dire ce qu'exige un système en production : CI/CD, monitoring, gestion des incidents.</li> <li>Vous avez déjà cadré et chiffré une solution, par exemple pour une proposition commerciale ou un plan projet.</li> <li>Vous avez défendu une architecture à la fois devant une direction métier ou un comité de direction, et devant les équipes sécurité et exploitation, en reliant la valeur business, les choix techniques et le plan de delivery.</li> </ol> <p><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Un plus, pas un prérequis :</span></p> <ul> <li>Architecture de plateformes agentiques : RAG, orchestration multi-agents, choix des technologies couche par couche.</li> <li>Gouvernance des données à l’échelle d’une grande entreprise : data mesh, gestion des accès.</li> <li>Plateformes on premise, hybrides ou souveraines, basées sur des technologies open source ou sur Kubernetes.</li> <li>Standards de run : SLA, PRA et PCA.</li> <li>Une expérience de CTO, de tech lead ou dans un rôle au contact des clients.</li> <li>Une certification d’architecture cloud.</li> <li>Une pratique régulière des coding agents.</li> </ul> <p>Ce poste n'est probablement pas pour vous si votre expertise porte sur une seule plateforme ou un seul éditeur et que vous souhaitez continuer à l'approfondir. Ni si construire et écrire du code est ce qui vous anime le plus : le rôle d'AI Applied Engineer vous correspondra mieux.</p> <p>Pas besoin de cocher toutes les cases pour postuler : si vous avez l’essentiel des indispensables et l’envie d’apprendre le reste, parlons-en.</p> <p><strong>Process de recrutement :</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>HR Interview (30-45 min) :</strong> Échange sur votre parcours, vos compétences managériales et l'adéquation culturelle avec un Talent Acquisition Specialist.</li> <li><strong>Architecture Case&nbsp; (60 min) :</strong> Session d'architecture avec un AI Architect basé en France sur un cas basé sur une vraie mission.</li> <li><strong>US / Manager Interview (60 min) :</strong> Échange avec un Director / Partner pour évaluer le fit managérial, opérationnel et la posture client.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Rémunération :</strong> Package :&nbsp; 75 000 € à 85 000 € brut annuel (fixe) + 8 000 € de variable, selon expérience et séniorité.</p> <p><strong>Présentation de l’entreprise</strong></p> <p>Artefact est un cabinet de conseil spécialisé en data et en intelligence artificielle, qui accompagne les entreprises pour transformer ces technologies en impact business concret et mesurable.</p> <p>A la croisée du conseil, de la data et de la technologie, nos 2 500 collaborateurs dans 27 pays mettent leurs expertises en commun pour concevoir, développer et déployer des solutions qui répondent aux enjeux de transformation de nos clients.</p> <p>Envie d'en savoir plus? Découvrez Artefact, nos expertises et notre culture : <a href="https://www.artefact.com/">https://www.artefact.com</a></p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><em>Chez Artefact, nous sommes convaincus que la diversité des parcours, des expériences et des perspectives fait la richesse de nos équipes. Nous nous engageons à offrir un environnement inclusif et des opportunités équitables, où chacune et chacun peut évoluer et exprimer pleinement son potentiel.
